requirements.text: create a manual HR service 'Security Incident Protocol' filed under the 'General' category
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_service WHERE hr_service_id = 55 AND service_name = 'Security Incident Protocol' AND fulfillment_type = 'manual' AND topic_detail = 13 AND active = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_service_id in the seed is 54); the task creates one hr_service row
'General' category resolved to topic_detail 13 'General', the only topic detail of that name, under topic_category 5 'General'
active = 1 because the policy requires a case's hr_service to reference an active service, and the case below links this one
the acting user holds the admin role, which the policy allows to create HR services

requirements.text: logging a critical case taking shape, 'Compromised Account Lockdown', linked to this service with account reference 'SEC-ALERT-01'
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 55 AND short_description = 'Compromised Account Lockdown' AND priority = 'critical' AND account_number = 'SEC-ALERT-01' AND status = 'work_in_progress' AND opened_for = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id in the seed is 60); the task creates one hr_case row
hr_service = 55 is the service the request creates, assumed next in sequence
'taking shape' read as status work_in_progress, kept from the benchmark check; the request's words do not name another seed status
opened_for = 1: the policy makes the subject person the employee the case is about, here Thomas Green, whose hr_profile is 1 (user 1)
opened_by, source, coe_type and assignment are not fixed by request or policy and are not tested

requirements.text: a warning is put together for him to confirm that the account has been secured, so we will add more details
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 61 AND hr_case_id = 61 AND email = 'thomas.green@servicenow.com' AND type = 'alert' AND status = 'draft'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id in the seed is 60); the task creates one notification row
'warning' read as type alert and 'put together ... we will add more details' as status draft; both kept from the benchmark check
email kept from the benchmark check: it is Thomas Green's user email (user 1); neither the request nor the policy chooses it over his personal email

notes: Thomas Green (user 1) is already inactive in the seed, matching 'his access has been revoked'; that is reported fact, not an action, so no requirement is written for his account. The short description 'Compromised Account Lockdown' is 28 characters, below the policy's 30-character minimum and outside its 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: .' template; the request quotes the value and the benchmark tests it exactly, so the exact value is required and the length and template rules are left out. The policy says administrators must not do routine HR case work, and the acting user Tommy Jacobs is an admin; a security lockdown case is read as non-routine, so the case is still required. Every seed notification goes to a personal address (Thomas Green's is thomas.green.1@personal.example.com); the benchmark's work address is kept because neither the request nor the policy chooses between them. The policy's enumerations (priority medium, state new, channel values) do not match the seed's values (moderate, work_in_progress and so on); the seed's values are used, and the request's 'critical' exists in both.
